title: fix(service-storage)!: enforce the storage settings Limits group (max_upload_mb, presigned_ttl, session_ttl) at the upload doors
body:
Fixes #22283
Clause-②: no (narrowing)

Setup's File Storage page renders a "Limits" group (`max_upload_mb`, `presigned_ttl`, `session_ttl`) and an admin's save persisted it, but nothing read it. This PR implements triage's direction ("honour the three keys at the doors that own them"; implement, not retire): `StorageServicePlugin` reads the group on every settings pass and every upload door honours it, on the plugin's own mount and on a host's `mountStorageRoutes` mount.

## What changed

- **`storage-limits.ts` (new, package-internal logic).** The one place the three keys are READ out of a `getNamespace('storage')` payload (`readStorageLimits`) and RESOLVED against a mount's own options (`resolveStorageLimits`). A numeric string is admitted because the settings service admits it for a `number` specifier; a present value that is not a positive number is not applied and is logged at `warn` naming the key and value.
- **`storage-service-plugin.ts`.** `applySettings` reads the Limits group on every pass, AHEAD of the adapter gate (that gate returns early when no adapter key is authored, and a save that touched only a limit must still land). The snapshot is held on the `SwappableStorageService` the plugin registers as `storage`, and `composeStorageRoutes` binds it for the doors from that service, so both mounts read it from the one place it is written, the same path an adapter save already takes. One `info` line names the snapshot when it changes.
- **`storage-routes.ts`.** Each request resolves the limits once (never hoisted to registration), so a save reaches the next request without a restart.
  - Size gate, before any row is written or byte stored: presigned door (declared `size`), chunked start (declared `totalSize`), local raw PUT (declared `content-length` before the body is read, then the bytes read), chunk door (bytes held so far plus this chunk, the same two ways).
  - The chunk door counts the latest recorded size per chunk index: both adapters replace a re-sent part, so a retried chunk is not counted twice. Each stored `parts` entry now records its `size`; a session whose parts predate that is judged by its running `uploaded_size`, the upper bound.
  - TTLs: presigned upload URLs and non-gated download URLs take the resolved `presignedTtl`; new chunked sessions take the resolved `sessionTtl`. Already-issued URLs and sessions keep the lifetime stamped at issue.
- **`swappable-storage-service.ts`**: `setLimitsSnapshot()` / `getLimitsSnapshot()`. **`index.ts`**: type exports `StorageLimitsSnapshot`, `StorageLimitReading`. **`mount-storage-routes.ts`**: option docs. README section, changeset.

## Measurements (H1 to H5 from the dispatch)

- **H1 holds.** At `238222d8`, non-test readers outside `service-settings`: `max_upload_mb` 0, `presigned_ttl` 0, `session_ttl` 0; controls in the same manifest `local_root` 4 files, `s3_bucket` 1 file. A settings change reaches the plugin through `settings.subscribe('storage', ...)`, which re-runs `applySettings`; the three keys now ride that path.
- **H2.** Manifest defaults vs the built-in defaults: `presigned_ttl` 3600 = 3600; `session_ttl` 86400 = 86400; `max_upload_mb` 100 vs no limit. So the one observable change with nothing saved is the 100 MB (104,857,600 bytes) cap; the changeset states it.
  - **Precedence: the seat's lead is falsified, and the measured behaviour is followed.** The adapter keys do NOT let the constructor win over a save: an authored save rebuilds the adapter over the constructor's (`buildAdapterFromValues`, "settings value wins over any constructor-provided local.rootDir"), while a manifest default never moves it (the authored-source gate). Followed per key: saved value (admin save or env override) wins over the host option (`presignedTtl` / `sessionTtl` on the constructor or on `mountStorageRoutes`), which wins over the namespace default, which wins over the built-in default. `max_upload_mb` has no host option.
- **H3, the code: the lead `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE` is not usable inside the fence.** The ledger lists it under `@objectstack/rest` only; `@objectstack/service-storage`'s row does not, so stamping it here would make `check:error-code-provenance` red, and the row lives in `packages/spec` (fenced out). The refusal is `413` with the standard member the platform itself derives for a 413 (`standardErrorCodeForHttpStatus(413)` is `VALIDATION_ERROR`; the catalog names no 413 member). No code was added. The message names the measured size, the limit in MB and bytes, and the setting key.
- **H3, the doors.** There is no single-request multipart door in `registerStorageRoutes`; the single-request path is presign plus the local adapter's raw PUT. On S3 the presigned PUT goes straight to the bucket, so that upload is judged by its declared size only (Acceptance notes).
- **H4, H5**: pinned below.

## Each door, before and after (status, code)

| Door | Before (no reader) | After, over the resolved limit | Stored on refusal |
|---|---|---|---|
| `POST upload/presigned` (declared `size`) | 200, pending `sys_file` row, URL minted | 413 `VALIDATION_ERROR` | nothing: `createFile` and `getPresignedUpload` not called |
| `POST upload/chunked` (declared `totalSize`) | 200, file + session rows, backend multipart | 413 `VALIDATION_ERROR` | nothing: `createFile`, `createSession`, `initiateChunkedUpload` not called |
| `PUT _local/raw/:token` (body) | 200, bytes stored | 413 `VALIDATION_ERROR` (by `content-length` before reading, and by bytes read) | nothing: `upload` not called, key absent on disk |
| `PUT upload/chunked/:id/chunk/:n` (held + chunk) | 200, chunk stored | 413 `VALIDATION_ERROR` (same two ways) | nothing: `uploadChunk` not called, `uploaded_size` unchanged |

The Before column is read from main's code (no reader of the key) and from ablations A1 to A4 below, where each door with its check removed answers 200 to the same over-limit request. At exactly the limit each door answers 200 (control in the same test). With no settings namespace bound (bare kernel, `bindToSettings: false`) no door limits (control: a 1 GiB declared size answers 200).

TTLs: with nothing saved, presigned URL 3600 s and session 86400 s before and after. With a saved `presigned_ttl` 120 and `session_ttl` 600: before 3600 / 86400 (saved value unread); after 120 (`expiresIn` and the token's `exp`, upload and non-gated download URLs) and 600 (`expiresAt`). A session issued before a save keeps its original `expiresAt`.

## Tests (final head `46d7554dc8`, `origin/main` `799eb000c7` merged in)

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-storage exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2`: 44 files, **736 passed**; this PR adds 19 of them (18 in the new `storage-limits.test.ts`, 1 in the envelope file).
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-storage typecheck`: exit 0, including `check:test-typecheck: OK` (both tsc programs list all 44 test files, the new one included, counted with `--listFiles`).
- Dogfood, real boot (`storage-upload-limits.dogfood.test.ts`, 2 cases; re-run at the final head with `field-file-collection`, `attachments-permission-matrix` and `route-ledger-live-mount-parity`: 34 passed, 1 declared skip; `@objectstack/dogfood` typecheck exit 0): nothing saved enforces 100 MB and 3600 s; `PUT /api/settings/storage {max_upload_mb: 1, presigned_ttl: 120}` reaches the doors without a restart, the presign refuses `1 MiB + 1`, the URL carries 120 s, and the raw PUT refuses a `1 MiB + 1` body and accepts exactly 1 MiB. **2 passed.**
- Consumer sweep at `73ce441fe8` (before the second merge), direction `...@objectstack/service-storage` (downstream), storage-touching files only: `organizations` 2 wall files 20 passed; `plugin-dev` 9 files 86 passed; `cli` unit tier, 4 storage files, 32 passed (its integration tier is declared to CI); dogfood, the 9 storage-touching files plus the new one, 93 passed, 1 skipped (the declared enterprise-package skip).
- `storage-limits.test.ts` sections: section 1, each door refuses over the limit with nothing stored, plus the retry and legacy-session chunk cases; section 2, TTLs and the precedence table; section 3, the plugin end to end through `applySettings` (defaults hold, saved values reach the doors, a save after boot reaches the next request while an issued session keeps its deadline, constructor TTL vs saved, `bindToSettings: false` control); section 4, `mountStorageRoutes` honours the snapshot and resolves the TTL against its host option. `error-envelope.conformance.test.ts` gains the 413 case.

## Ablations (each committed first; restore proven against `HEAD`; run at `071760b844`..`102ce46155`, which the two `main` merges did not touch)

Mutations went through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (anchor must hit once; blob change and restore proven on disk; `git diff HEAD` empty after every leg). The unit pins import `src/` relatively, so no build or dist preflight is involved there.

| Leg | Mutation | Red |
|---|---|---|
| A1 | presign size check removed | 5: presign door, envelope 413 case, defaults-hold, saved-values, host door |
| A2 | chunked-start check removed | 2: chunked start, save-after-boot |
| A3 / A3b | raw PUT bytes check / `content-length` pre-check removed | 1 each |
| A4 / A4b | chunk bytes check / `content-length` pre-check removed | 1 each |
| A5 | plugin no longer stores the snapshot | 4 (section 3 except the `bindToSettings: false` control) |
| A6 | composition no longer binds the snapshot | 5 (section 3 and section 4) |
| A7 | saved value no longer beats the host option | 2 |
| R1 | chunk door counts the running total again | 1: the retry case |
| R2 | legacy-session branch removed | 1: the legacy case |
| D1 (dogfood, through `dist/`) | size gate answers "within" for everything; built; `ablation-dist-preflight` marker present in `dist/index.js` and `dist/index.cjs` | 2 of 2 dogfood cases ("expected 200 to be 413"); restored, rebuilt, preflight `--absent` exit 0, rerun 2 passed |

D1's first attempt was void and is not counted: its marker was a comment (stripped by the bundler) and its replacement broke the DTS build, so `dist/` never carried it. It was redone with a string-literal marker that type-checks.

## Gates

`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` at `46d7554dc8`: 71 commands, the same list as at `73ce441fe8` and `102ce46155`. All were run at the final head, plus `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec run check:error-code-provenance` (the reason for the code choice). Verdicts are in the dispatch report on the card. The error-envelope and code families (`check:route-envelope`, `check:dispatcher-error-vocabulary`, `check:error-code-provenance`) are green.

Lint, narrowed and proven: `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` over all 11 changed paths at `46d7554dc8`. eslint's own config lints 9 of them and ignores the two markdown files ("no matching configuration"). Result: 9 linted, 0 errors, 0 warnings. `eslint.config.mjs` enables no type-aware linting (no `parserOptions.project`, no `projectService`), so this diff cannot move the verdict of an untouched file. The full `pnpm lint` run is CI's.

## Acceptance notes

- **S3 presigned uploads are judged by declared size only.** The bytes go to the bucket directly; binding the size into the signature needs a `StorageUploadOptions` field in the spec contract (fenced out here). The local adapter's byte door judges real bytes. Not filed: not measured against a live bucket.
- **Pre-existing: the chunk door's `uploaded_size` / `uploaded_chunks` double-count a retried chunk index.** Measured on this branch's build with no limit: a 1 MiB session whose 600 KiB chunk 0 is sent twice reports `uploadedSize` 1228800 and `percentComplete` 100 while holding 600 KiB. This PR fixed only the part it touched: the size limit no longer counts a retry twice (without that fix the retry was refused 413 while holding 600 KiB). The progress accounting itself is unchanged and is handed to the seat as a finding.
- The commit door (`POST upload/complete`) does not re-measure stored bytes; the declared size was judged at presign.
- **Pre-existing, untouched here: a resumed chunked upload can commit without its earlier chunks.** Measured on this branch's build through the doors, in the order the SDK's `resumeUpload` drives them (progress, then the chunks from `uploadedChunks` on, then completion listing only those parts): a 2-chunk upload whose chunk 0 (5 MiB) was stored in the first pass commits with `200` and `size` 5242890 while the stored file is 10 bytes. The completion door assembles only the parts the request lists. Handed to the seat as a finding.
- `plugin-email`'s inbound attachment storage writes through `storage.upload` server-side; it is not an upload door and is not capped.
- Out of the fence and untouched: which organization an upload belongs to, the uploader-ownership checks, the organization-change answers, `packages/spec`, the settings manifest.

> Seat's append (`domain:services` seat 1, #6021), carried verbatim from the dev's round-2 report `6063587901` (with the dev's one stated correction: 25 to 32 minutes); the dev never edits a PR body.

## Round 2 (seat review, R1)

- **R1: `check:error-status-conformance` was red on `46d7554dc8`.** Per the ruling, this PR ships `413` `VALIDATION_ERROR` (option A). The switch to `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE` is carried by #22314. The 413 is now documented as an exception to the code's 400, mirroring how `MISSING_REQUIRED_FIELD` documents its 422.
  - `content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx`: a callout in the `VALIDATION_ERROR` section, and a 413 exception row in the HTTP Status Quick Reference ("this row is an exception to the 400 row, not a second home for the code").
  - `content/docs/protocol/kernel/error-handling.mdx`: `**HTTP Status:** 400 — with one documented exception, which answers **413** (see below)`, a "the one 413" bullet under Where it comes from, and a 413 row in the HTTP Status Codes table.
  - Every added line names the storage upload doors and `max_upload_mb`, so the switch removes exactly these lines. Once `VALIDATION_ERROR` is no longer emitted at 413, the gate's direction B goes red on any line left behind.
- **Which page the gate needs.** Measured at `736713afc8` with proven-restore ablations: either page's claim is enough on its own.
  - Catalog row removed: green, 29 pairs.
  - Protocol status line reduced to 400: green, 29 pairs.
  - Both removed: red, 1 finding, 28 pairs.
  - Before the docs (`46d7554dc8`) the gate was red with the CI finding. After: `✓ every derivable runtime status is documented, and every documented status is reachable`, 29 (code, status) pairs.
- **Why the derivation did not name this gate.** `dispatch-gates` places `check:error-status-conformance` only by four file literals: `errors.zod.ts`, the two doc pages and its baseline.
  - The gate walks `packages/**` through `const SCAN_ROOT = 'packages'` (`scripts/check-error-status-conformance.mjs:222`, walked at `:2099`). That is a bare single-segment literal, and the hint extractor refuses those by design.
  - So for a diff under `packages/**` the gate sat in the artifact-roster block, silent and outside the 71 commands. With this round's doc paths it is matched, and it is now one of the 97.
  - Reported to the seat as a finding; no gate added.
- **CI.**
  - On `46d7554dc8`, `Test Core (1/6)` was cancelled at 15:20:41 when the round-2 push superseded the run. It had run 19 minutes; the shard takes 25 to 32 minutes on recent `main` runs. The aggregate `Test Core` then reported a missing shard attestation, not a test failure.
  - On `736713afc8`: `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Build Core`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Temporal Conformance` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` succeeded, as did Test Core 2 to 6. `Test Core (1/6)` was still in progress at report time.
- **Local verification at `736713afc8`.**
  - Derivation: 97 families (the docs added 26); all run, plus `check:error-code-provenance`, 98 of 98 exit 0. `--ran` reconciliation: 97 of 97, 0 NOT-MEASURED.
  - `service-storage`: 736 passed. Typecheck: exit 0. Dogfood storage-limits file: 2 passed.
